To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new plasmids-encoded pathogenicity isalnd was detected in ETEC strains from weaned pigs producing F18 fimiabriae.

(i) we describe a new plasmids encoded pathogenicity island, which contains the stb gene and which has been designated pTC; (ii) the pTC plasmid is present in most F-18+ enterotoxin and verotoxin producing E. coli strains isolated from weaned pigs; and (iii) pTC is not present in F-4+ ETEC strains
we have identified a new plasmids-encoded pathogenicity islands, which is present in most of the F18+ EEC and F18+ VTEC, which are the main pathogens of postweaning diarrhea in pigs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of a new plmasmid-encoded PAI in ETEC and VTEC strains from pigs.
the molecular analysis of virulence plasmids in ETEC and their pathogenicity islands (PAIs) and their possible role in pathogenicity.
the molecular characterisation of a new plamid-encoded pathogenic island that is present in ETEC/VETEC strains of weaned pigs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 40-kb pTC-like PAI is characteristic of the F18+ EETC/VTEC and the 10-kb pTC TSL is characteristic of F18+ EEC.
the Tn1681-sta gene is located on a 40-kbp pathogenicity island which is flanked by IS elements at both sides.
the 40-kb PAI is characteristic of F18-producing ETEC and VTEC strains, but not of all strains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TSL is a new plasmidspecific virulence island in F18 ETEC and VTEC strains.
we found that a plasmid of an F18+ ETC strain from Germany contained a new pathogenicity island that could be mobilised into another plasmid.
a plasmid of 120-kb (pTC) was isolated from a porcine E. coli strain (strain 2173) that produces the F18 fimbrial adhesion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stb gene of porcine E. coli can be used as a genetic marker to identify F4 and F18 ETEC strains.

a novel plasmid-encoded virulence island has been identified in ETEC strains that produce F18 fimbriae and is associated with the production of enterotoxins (ETEC), verotoxin (ETEC/VETEC), and fimbriation.
the F18+ EHEC/VTEC isolates are more likely to be associated with a pathogenicity island, while the F4+ isolates are more often associated with the Tn452-like stb type.
